idiom_name: companion-object factory function + private primary constructor with require() validation
implementation_notes: Kotlin constructors cannot be named and cannot return a typed failure, so the idiomatic factory is a function in the companion object (or a top-level factory function) that validates with require()/requireNotNull() and then delegates to a private primary constructor; single-value products use an @JvmInline value class whose init block enforces the invariant on every construction path, including Java interop. What replaces the classic factory class is the factory function colocated with the type; keep an injected factory class when creation needs repositories or domain services, since constructors cannot suspend.
pitfalls: A data class would generate a public copy() that re-creates the instance without the factory's rules; use a plain class with a private constructor for invariant-bearing aggregates.
Secondary constructors must delegate to the primary constructor, so validation in the init block still runs - but a named factory function keeps the failure explicit and the call site readable.
Suspending creation (repository lookups) cannot happen in a constructor or init block; use a suspend factory function or a standalone factory class.
